QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_44

question.text: Value at Risk (VaR) has which of the following limitations?

answer.text: It indicates the exact size of loss beyond the confidence threshold
It tells investors nothing about the probability of loss
It does NOT tell you the size of loss in the tail beyond the confidence level (for that, use CVaR / Expected Shortfall)

explanation.text: The Logic: VaR quantifies the maximum loss at a confidence level but says NOTHING about how bad the loss could be in the tail beyond that level. Conditional VaR (CVaR) / Expected Shortfall fills that gap by averaging losses beyond the VaR threshold. The Trap: A is opposite of truth. B is wrong — VaR DOES tie probability to loss. D is too specific. Cross-Exam Context: VIII Equity Derivatives, III-A/C Compliance, XIX-E all test VaR. CVaR is specifically XIX-E Cat III focus given tail-heavy hedge-fund returns. Manager's Pro-Tip: Augment VaR with stress tests (e.g., 2008 crisis, 2020 COVID shock re-run on current portfolio). A single VaR number is blind to regime shifts.
